THOUGHT: Elderly man with recent COVID-19 then 2 weeks of headache and acute right visual loss with painful eye movement. CT shows complete right sinus opacification and bone erosion of the medial orbital apex with extension into the apex — an orbital‑apex process producing visual loss. Sinus culture grew Streptococcus constellatus (a member of the anginosus/“microabscess” group) but the key diagnostic data are markedly elevated serum IgG4 and tissue histology showing a dense plasma‑cell infiltrate with 50–100 IgG4+ plasma cells per high‑power field and most IgG+ cells being IgG4+. This pattern is diagnostic for IgG4‑related disease (IgG4‑RD) involving the sinonasal/orbital region (an IgG4‑related inflammatory pseudotumor) causing bone erosion and orbital‑apex syndrome, with secondary bacterial superinfection possible. Other considerations include complicated bacterial sinusitis with orbital extension, invasive fungal rhinosinusitis (post‑viral predisposition), neoplasm of the sinonasal/orbital region, and granulomatous/vasculitic disease such as GPA, but the histopathology and serum IgG4 make IgG4‑RD by far the most likely.

DIAGNOSIS:
1. IgG4‑related disease (IgG4‑related chronic rhinosinusitis / orbital inflammatory pseudotumor with extension to the orbital apex) — strongest fit: elderly man, high serum IgG4, tissue with abundant IgG4+ plasma cells, mass‑like sinonasal lesion with bone erosion and orbital apex involvement.
2. Complicated acute bacterial rhinosinusitis with orbital‑apex extension (osteomyelitis/subperiosteal abscess) due to Streptococcus constellatus — supported by positive sinus culture and acute symptoms; likely a secondary/superimposed infection.
3. Invasive fungal rhinosinusitis (mucormycosis/aspergillosis) with orbital/apical involvement — important post‑viral differential given rapid visual loss and bone destruction, but less likely because fungal elements not reported and histology favors IgG4.
4. Sinonasal malignancy (e.g., squamous cell carcinoma, extranodal lymphoma/MALT or NK/T‑cell lymphoma) with orbital invasion — can produce bone erosion and mass‑like infiltrates; histology and IgG4 staining make this less likely but remains a critical alternative.
5. Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (Wegener) or other granulomatous/vasculitic orbital inflammatory disease (or Tolosa‑Hunt syndrome) — can cause destructive sinonasal disease and orbital apex syndrome; however, characteristic necrotizing granulomas/vasculitis or supporting serologies are not present and IgG4 findings point away from this.
ground_truth: IgG4-related rhinosinusitis with concurrent Streptococcus constellatus bacterial rhinosinusitis
